rules.pinpoint: Chapter 1, How Much Can Be Contributed?
rules.interpretation: 2025 only. Regular traditional and Roth contributions share the annual limit. Compensation is checked separately; no spousal compensation rule is modeled.

rules.pinpoint: Chapter 1, How Much Can Be Contributed?
rules.interpretation: Age at the end of 2025; the catch-up limit is 8000 dollars, not the different 2026 limit.

rules.pinpoint: Chapter 1, How Much Can Be Contributed? and Nondeductible Contributions
rules.interpretation: A conditional amount-limit check. Scope supplies timely eligible contributions and designation as nondeductible. No deduction, direct-Roth MAGI test, spousal IRA rule, or overall tax optimization is inferred.
Prior basis is supplied from records, never inferred to be zero from missing Form 8606. Scope excludes basis adjustments and other current-year deductible traditional contributions.
2025-designated contributions made January 1 through April 15, 2026 are removed from basis available for 2025 conversions. No disaster-deadline relief is modeled.

rules.pinpoint: Part I, lines 6-9; traditional IRA definition above Part I
rules.interpretation: Scope requires the owner's combined traditional, traditional SEP and traditional SIMPLE IRA balances at all custodians. No spouse's IRA or employer 401(k) balance. Line 7 and special line 6 adjustments are zero by explicit scope assumption.

rules.pinpoint: Part I, lines 10-11; Part II, line 17
rules.interpretation: Exact rational allocation capped at one, then rounded once to nearest cent with ties up. This is an allocation estimate, not a completed Form 8606: the form permits a decimal ratio rounded to at least three places and filing rounding can differ. The arithmetic convention is explicit and requires independent formalization review.
Amount included in income estimate, not tax owed. Rates, penalties, credits, Medicare effects, state taxes and future Roth withdrawals are outside scope.
Includes 2025-designated contributions made in early 2026. No other distributions or adjustments; shares the allocation rounding convention.

rules.pinpoint: Part I, lines 11 and 14; Part II, line 18
rules.interpretation: Summarizes one bounded conditional calculation. IRS guidance is classified as administrative guidance, with persuasive model assessments rather than binding legislation. Neither input authenticity nor legal fidelity is established by proof replay.
